circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, designed by Hermann Tilke, and has been the venue for Formula One's season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street course that winds around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds an FIA Grade 1 licence. It serves as the venue for the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix, alongside various support racing categories including the Supercars Championship event.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km motorsport venue that has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods in Formula One history. Originally known as the Österreichring, it held the race for 18 consecutive years starting in 1970 before being redesigned and renamed the A1-Ring to accommodate the Grand Prix once more from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Located alongside Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan's capital, the Baku City Circuit is a street track measuring 6. 003 km per lap, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted Formula One racing in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming a permanent fixture on the calendar the following year with the debut Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted Formula One's inaugural Middle Eastern Grand Prix and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside other motorsport series. The FIA Grade 1-licensed facility has accommodated various racing formats including drag racing, GP2 competition, and endurance events, while also featuring multiple track configurations for different racing disciplines.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced layout combining extended straightaways with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Belgian Ardennes near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a staple of international motorsport since hosting the first Belgian Grand Prix in 1925. The venue has appeared on the Formula One calendar since the sport's inaugural season in 1950 and has maintained continuous annual hosting of the Belgian Grand Prix since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Situated on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary track that serves as the host venue for the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the circuit has accommodated various racing series including international sportscar competitions, open-wheel championships, and stock car events throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 through 2019 before resuming in 2024, establishing itself as the premier venue for Formula One racing in the country. The track has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing events beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone Circuit, located in Northamptonshire, England, became the inaugural venue for the World Championship of Drivers when it hosted the British Grand Prix in 1950. After sharing the British Grand Prix with other English circuits between 1955 and 1986, Silverstone secured the race as its permanent home from 1987 onwards. The venue also stages international motorcycle racing events on its grounds.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: Located in Mogyoród near Budapest, the Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted Formula One's inaugural race behind the Iron Curtain in 1986, chosen over a proposed Monaco-style street course in the city's largest park. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Grand Prix venue at the time, the track inaugurated its first race on 24 March 1986 as a tribute to Hungary's pioneering motorcycle racing champion János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 that ranks among Europe's pioneering purpose-built racing venues. The track has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, making it one of the most enduring Formula One fixtures, and earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" from its notably fast layout featuring extended straights and high-velocity turns.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, spans 5. 807 kilometers and is operated by a Honda subsidiary. The 155,000-capacity venue has become iconic for hosting Formula One World Championship races and Japanese Super Formula competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard. The 3. 8-mile layout weaves past iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues, including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment in the heart of the city's hospitality district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two Mexican racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted the Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, most recently as a continuous fixture since 2015 on its current layout, following earlier hosting periods that concluded in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that hosts the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the F1 calendar in 2022. The 3. 363-mile track features 19 corners and achieves average qualifying speeds near 139 mph, having been designed by Apex Circuit Design.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the waterfront of Monaco's harbour. Though officially recognized as the Circuit de Monaco, it is popularly known as Monte Carlo since most of the route traverses that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track known for its dramatic elevation changes and steeply banked corners that wind through the seaside landscape. The venue hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026, earning the nickname "The Roller coaster in the Dunes" from fans due to its unique topography featuring turns like Tarzan and Hugenholtz that create an exhilarating racing experience.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a motorsport venue situated north of Doha in Qatar, stretching 5. 419 kilometers with a prominent 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, originally opened in 1940 and renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and also houses a kart facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has served as the venue for the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021, while also hosting international electric racing events from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through central Singapore around Marina Bay, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km motorsport venue features a diverse mix of straights and corner configurations that make it suitable for testing a wide range of racing skills. Holding an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodating over 140,000 spectators, the circuit serves as a prominent venue for international motorsport competitions.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 track that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the facility regularly hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP and endurance racing competitions, while having previously accommodated various other racing series ranging from IndyCar to rallycross.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai-British driver Alexander Albon represents Thailand in Formula One racing, currently driving for the Williams team.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships in 2005 and 2006 during his tenure with Renault and secured 32 race victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond the sport's premier category, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including triumphs at Le Mans with Toyota and victories in the World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both a Formula One drivers' title and a World Endurance drivers' championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver for Mercedes, claimed the 2026 Formula One World Drivers' Championship at the youngest age in history. Since entering the sport in 2025, he has secured nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One, currently racing for the Audi team. Known for his competitive performances in the sport, he represents one of the grid's international talent pool.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas is a Finnish driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One. The experienced competitor twice came second in the drivers' championship during his Mercedes years in 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 race victories throughout his 13-season career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with Alpine. The South American driver pursues his career in the premier motorsport series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian motorsport competitor currently racing in the LMP2 category of the Asian Le Mans Series with AF Corse, while simultaneously holding a reserve driver position at Haas in Formula One. The driver has made appearances at seven Formula One events between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly represents France in Formula One racing, currently driving for Alpine. The French competitor achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian driver who represents France in Formula One while competing for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven Formula One world championships, equalling Michael Schumacher's record. He also holds multiple all-time records including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, capturing the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, currently drives for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished as the runner-up in the 2022 championship and has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, known as K-Mag, has raced in Formula One across two separate periods from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship, driving for WRT in a factory BMW program.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently competing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Throughout his eight-season career, he has secured 14 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, most recently drove for Haas in Formula One. The highlight of his career came in 2021 when he secured victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix while racing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Checo Pérez, a Mexican driver currently competing for Cadillac, finished second in the 2023 World Drivers' Championship while racing for Red Bull. Over his 15 seasons in Formula One, he has claimed victories in six Grand Prix events.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri competes in Formula One for McLaren, where he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport over four seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, claiming eight Grand Prix victories during his career before retiring from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Mercedes, having secured eight race victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the World Endurance Championship, where he will drive for Ford after previously racing in the LMGT3 category with Proton Competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver who currently races for Aston Martin, competing at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese motorsport competitor, currently holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After competing as a full-time driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a reserve role beginning in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen competes for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, where he has claimed four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season career, he has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the sport from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He currently maintains his connection to Formula One in a support capacity with the American team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based outfit has competed as Alpine since 2021, representing Renault's sports car division and serving as the manufacturer's official works team until Renault's withdrawal at the conclusion of 2025. Previously operating under the Renault F1 Team banner, the squad underwent rebranding to align with the Alpine marque's motorsport ambitions while maintaining its connection to the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One across multiple eras as a British manufacturer, with its current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian automaker Ferrari, is motorsport's most enduring and accomplished outfit, participating in every Formula One World Championship from 1950 onwards. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" for their iconic emblem, the team has established itself as the sport's most successful operation throughout its seven-decade history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the team commenced racing in 2016 with a focus on competitive entry-level operations. Leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role from long-serving Guenther Steiner, who had directed the squad since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing outfit founded in 1970, Sauber initially competed in endurance motorsport before entering Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. The team established itself as one of the sport's longest-running entrants, though it underwent numerous transformations across three decades before being acquired by Audi in 2024 and subsequently departing Formula One in 2025.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship arrangements. The team operates as part of the larger McLaren Group, which is controlled by Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a continuous presence in Formula One since 1954 through team ownership and engine supply roles. The current iteration, based in Brackley and licensed under the German flag, became a tri-owned entity in 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff. The marque's racing heritage is traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as the second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a Milton Keynes facility, the team operates as a sister squad within the Red Bull Formula One structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two teams under Red Bull ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the squad represents the second constructor within the Austrian conglomerate's racing portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing operates as a Formula One team under an Austrian licence from its English base, forming part of the Red Bull GmbH automotive portfolio alongside Racing Bulls. Since its 2005 establishment, the team was led by Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, with Laurent Mekies assuming the leadership role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes under various title sponsorships, including Atlassian Williams for the 2026 season, and has established itself as a significant force in the sport's history.
